rule: CANDIDATE SET = files of the admitted php population whose TEXT contains `#[` (a SUPERSET of the files that can carry a PHP attribute: `#[` is required and contiguous, and a comment/string containing it only adds a file that parses to zero attributes). Every candidate is PARSED; the decisive counter classifies each DIRECT argument expression of each `attribute` node by its own node type.

decoratesCounter.preRegisteredPredicate: an `attribute` whose ARGUMENT is a call-shaped expression

samples: phpunit/tests/end-to-end/_files/data-provider/ClosureDuplicateStringKeyTest.php: anonymous_function: static function (): Generator { yield 'key' => [true]; yield 'key' => [false]; }
phpunit/tests/end-to-end/_files/data-provider/ClosureThrowsExceptionTest.php: anonymous_function: static function (): array { throw new RuntimeException('closure failed'); }

decoratesCounter.meaning: `directCallShaped` IS the pre-registered counter: non-zero falsifies the passive-metadata ruling and `decorates` is implemented. `callableArgument` (a closure passed as a metadata VALUE) and `nestedCallOnly` (a call shape somewhere beneath the argument) are reported because the FIRST implementation of the counter walked the whole `arguments` subtree and therefore measured `nestedCallOnly` while claiming to measure the predicate.

screens.note: a candidate set that misses a file reports a clean zero over a population it never read — the control above is what prevents that
